correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 34–70. Planck prefactors cancel at each wavelength, giving r_j=(s^k−1)/(t^k−1), k=4,2,1. For t>s>1, r_2/r_3=(s+1)/(t+1)<1 and r_1/r_2=(s²+1)/(t²+1)<1, so reciprocal depths order strictly when β>0. Factoring the two differences gives F_s(t)=(s+1)(s+t)/(1+t²); differentiation and endpoints give the strictly decreasing bijection onto (0,2s(s+1)/(1+s²)). In this interval R<s(s+1), so the quadratic has negative constant and positive leading coefficient: the plus radical is the only positive root, and the range calculation ensures t>s. Recovering β from the last two reciprocals and α from either of them matches the first via the same ratio. The equations f=β/(α+β), δ=1/(α+β) give the exact interior constraints β>0 and α>1; strict ordering already gives β>0. With any two distinct channels the two affine coefficients vary continuously as t varies, retaining the strict inequalities in a neighborhood, so the ambiguity is indeed local at every interior point. Even for arbitrary distinct monochromatic wavelengths the contrasts differ: with κ=T_star/T_c>1, log((e^x−1)/(e^(κx)−1)) has derivative [g(x)−g(κx)]/x<0, g(x)=x/(1−e^(−x)) increasing for x>0. Achromatic endpoints lose the spot information as stated. The s=2,t=3 example gives differences 75/16 and 25/8, R=3/2 and (α,β)=(75,25). I inspected checker.py without executing it; the synthetic runs reported by the record are not a proof of its all-parameter claim.

value.rationale: This gives one simple exact model in which observers can distinguish structural two-band ambiguity from an invertible three-band diagnostic. The geometric wavelengths give a factorization that proves global rather than local identification and make rejection of incompatible positive triples possible. The strict α bound has the physical meaning that the planet is smaller than the available photospheric area. Value is as a noiseless identifiability and feasibility benchmark, not an instrument-ready estimator or an assertion about arbitrary wavelength triples.
